summary:
Every rating in the shop is running hot, and hitting is the category carrying the model right now: R4's hitting cell is up +11.2pts over baseline (62% in the last 14, n=80, 4-game win streak), R1 sits at +11.9pts with its own 3W streak, and R3's hitting mark has pushed a 4-game streak at 59%. Trends remains the steadiest performer across all four ratings — identical 52-28 (65%) last-14 lines and +8.9pts hot flags across R1-R3, plus R4 matching that exact split against its smaller season sample. Strong-play units confirm the heat is real, not noise: R4 is the standout at 14d 25-9 (74%, +24.0u) and 30d 66-38 (63%, +39.0u), with R3 close behind at 14d 24-9 (73%, +19.0u). Trends+sp remains the top agreement combo all year at 57.9% (n=620), and with trends hot across the board right now, any slate where sp and trends line up together deserves extra weight.

Today's board is thin — just PHI @ ATL — but the signal is clean. All four ratings converge on ATL, with R4 showing the strongest lean (+0.72) and R3 close behind (+0.74), both of which are riding the hottest category (hitting) and the best strong-play unit trends in the shop right now. PHI as a model-liked team sits at a modest 57% (25-19, n=44) with strong plays going 12-6 (+4.0u) — nothing special — while ATL isn't in the top-teams table at all, meaning this lean is coming from the rating engines' internal signal rather than a team-specific edge. With SP still TBD for both sides, lean on R4 and R3 here since they're both posting +24.0u and +19.0u over the last 14 days respectively and carry the hottest hitting/runs combos in the system. Full consensus with no fade from any rating is rare and worth respecting, especially with R4's 63% 30-day strong-play clip backing the lean. No disagreement to monitor since every rating landed in the same direction — this is as clean a single-game night as the model offers.
